text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.6% today as oil prices tumbled below $100 a barrel on growing hopes for diplomatic resolution in the Middle East—specifically, reports that Trump is open to talks with Iran. While geopolitical tensions remain high (Houthi attacks, the Strait of Hormuz still closed, and damage near Saudi infrastructure), the market is pricing in the possibility of reduced conflict and a return to more normal supply flows, which would ease the oil scarcity that has been supporting prices.

The broader context here is the volatile two-week slide of 4.4%: the stock has been swinging sharply as traders struggle to price in the competing risks—genuine supply disruptions from the Saudi pipeline shutdown and regional instability on one side, but signs of diplomatic off-ramps that could deflate oil prices on the other. For a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly hit revenues and margins, even if those lower prices come from easing crisis risk rather than declining global demand.
